name: High Push-Up Position Plank
description: The high push-up position plank is a foundational isometric core stability exercise in which the body is held in a rigid, straight line from head to heel while supported on the hands and toes. Compared to the forearm plank, the extended-arm position places greater demand on the shoulder girdle stabilizers and serratus anterior, while the core musculature functions identically to maintain spinal stiffness. It is a prerequisite position for push-up and many other calisthenic progressions and should be mastered before advancing to dynamic variations.

execution.starting_position: Place the hands on the floor directly under the shoulders. Extend the legs behind, toes on the floor. The body forms a straight line from head to heel.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Use a mat for wrist comfort on hard surfaces.
steps: Step 1: Position hands under shoulders, fingers spread for grip.
Step 2: Drive the floor away — imagine pushing the ground down. Protract the scapulae slightly.
Step 3: Squeeze the glutes and brace the core. Lock out the knees.
Step 4: Keep the body in a straight line — no hip hiking, sagging, or piking.
Step 5: Hold for the target duration, maintaining perfect alignment throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously with shallow breaths. Do not hold the breath.
common_mistakes: Hips piking up — this reduces core demand and places it on the shoulders
Hips sagging — this compresses the lumbar spine under load
safety_considerations: Avoid if wrist pain is present — substitute forearm plank
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Isometric hold. Perfect alignment must be maintained for the full duration.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Hold for target time: beginners 20–30 s; intermediate 45–60 s; advanced 60–90 s+.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the glutes — the whole posterior chain is a unit
Long spine — from crown to heel
